label: Attached
title: Attached
summary: Add a subordinate signal to a main item without altering its footprint.
corePrinciple: Attachment supports the item, never obscures it.

anatomy.title: A small signal stays attached to its main item
anatomy.description: Attached keeps a subordinate badge connected to the content it qualifies. The badge can straddle an edge or corner without changing the main item’s layout footprint.
blocks: The child in the main slot establishes the size and the visual object people identify first.
The badge slot is centered on the selected anchor and can straddle the main edge.
Position chooses one of nine anchors; the token ring separates a compact signal from the main mark.

configuration.title: Choose the anchor and corner relationship
configuration.description: Use the exposed position choices for where the badge belongs. For diagonal anchors, choose the round child’s edge or its bounding-box corner.
blocks: Place the signal where it belongs
Use edge or corner anchors when the badge describes the item. A center anchor is reserved for a deliberate overlay.
The child stays a native circular capsule in both examples. Corner projection changes only the badge anchor: use Circle edge for round marks and Bounding box for a square corner relationship.

states.title: The composition state belongs to its children
states.description: Attached has no loading or disabled state of its own. Show whether a supporting signal is present through its children.
blocks: The secondary signal remains visible while the main item keeps its own identity.
Use the same composition when there is no subordinate status or action to show.

sizing.title: Make room for the part that overhangs
sizing.description: The main child owns its intrinsic size. Attached does not grow the layout footprint for the badge, so its host needs enough whitespace for the overhang.
blocks: Whitespace keeps the edge signal clear.

content.title: Keep the attachment subordinate
content.description: Use a compact, meaningful signal that clarifies the main item. The badge should not carry the primary label or become a second focal point.
blocks: Make the main item readable first
The badge adds a small qualification such as payment type or status while the central mark remains easy to recognize.
Choose a familiar icon or small signal that people can understand at a glance.
A centered badge covers the main mark, so use it only when the overlay itself is the intended message.

inContext.title: Attach a qualifier to a real list item
inContext.description: A payment row keeps the qualifier next to the item it describes.
blocks: A small secondary signal stays attached to the item it qualifies.

doDont.title: Let the signal support the item
doDont.description: Each comparison shows a visible consequence of treating the attachment as supporting information.
blocks: Anchor a small badge to the edge when the main icon carries the identity.
A centered badge obscures the item it is meant to qualify.
The main mark remains the first thing people can identify.
Leave slack around the composition so the badge can straddle the edge.
Overflow hidden turns a positioning choice into a visibly cut-off signal.
The host needs space beyond the main bounds.
Use a small, familiar symbol for supporting information.
An oversized attachment pulls focus away from the main item.
Secondary signals should stay visually lighter than the main item.

sources.title: Grounded in the public attachment contract
sources.description: This guide uses the published Attached API, the Coin Components Library node, and the canonical Storybook fixtures.
blocks: Default, all positions, corner, and capsule badge stories

Examples use public Attached and IconCapsule exports from jfs-components 0.1.78. The package defaults circular to true; the guide uses that default when omitted and exposes the supported choice. Badge placement waits for layout measurement, and the badge does not expand the parent layout footprint. The capsule story enlarges its children with style dimensions; this guide uses the native Icon Capsule Size modes M and XS so both child capsules keep their component-owned circular geometry.
